raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes #60587

DeepSeek-V4 with a block-FP8 checkpoint fails at engine init when `--linear-backend` forces a non-DeepGEMM FP8 kernel, for example `--linear-backend marlin`. The error is a `torch.bmm` shape error in `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj`. This change picks the kernel again for block-FP8 `is_bmm` layers after loading. On CUDA, `wo_a` then always gets the DeepGEMM layout that the O-projection reads.

Compared with #56119, this fix:

- Fixes the other forced backends too, not only Marlin: [#56119](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56119) guards only the Marlin case. On its tree, `humming` still fails with the issue's 4x shape error, and `triton` and `cutlass` fail with `t.dim() == N`. All of them pass with this change.
- Keeps `wo_a` in FP8: [#56119](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56119) runs `wo_a` as a bf16 copy through `torch.bmm`. On the reproducer below, that leaves 0.75 GiB less KV cache per GPU (65.97 vs 66.72 GiB with FlashMLA, 66.33 vs 67.08 GiB with FlashInfer).
- Tests the path that failed: The new test builds a real block-FP8 layer and runs `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj`. It fails on the old code with the issue's error. The regression test in [#56119](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56119) uses a fake Marlin kernel and checks only the weight dtype.
- Is smaller and reuses existing kernel selection: It adds 29 lines in `vllm/` against 76. It picks the kernel again after loading, as the ModelOpt MXFP8 path already does, and adds no new dequantize helper that repeats `scaled_dequantize()`.


## Claims

- `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp` with `--linear-backend marlin` now starts and serves. Both attention paths named in the issue work: the default (FlashMLA) and `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`. Before, engine init failed in the memory-profiling forward pass.
- The same change fixes `humming`, `triton` and `cutlass` as forced backends. They broke `wo_a` in the same way.
- All other linear layers still use the requested backend. Only `wo_a` takes DeepGEMM. The model never calls `wo_a`'s own kernel. It only reads its weight.
- A new unit test covers this. It fails on the old code with the issue's error.

## Validation

Setup: 2 x NVIDIA B200 in one machine (TP=2), driver 610.19, CUDA 13.3, torch 2.13.0+cu130. vLLM commit `81198e97ba7eee2a22540caaa756b7fdddcb4d93`, then the same commit plus this change. Weights: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp`, revision `6821d6ad3681a4b137b066b76094fa82ebd0a380`. The issue used 2 x GB10 (SM 12.1). This was not run on GB10.

Reproducer. No request is needed, because it fails during startup:

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --max-model-len 524288 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --enable-prefix-caching \
  --load-format safetensors --moe-backend marlin --linear-backend marlin \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
```

Before (on both TP workers):

```
File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py", line 501, in forward
    return self._o_proj(attn_out, positions)
File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/flashmla.py", line 62, in _o_proj
    return deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj(
File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/o_proj.py", line 98, in deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj
    torch.bmm(
RuntimeError: Expected size for first two dimensions of batch2 tensor to be: [4, 4096] but got: [4, 1024].
```

After:

```
(Worker_TP0 pid=2338534) INFO 10-09 05:03:03 [__init__.py:747] Selected MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel for Fp8LinearMethod
(Worker_TP0 pid=2338534) WARNING 10-09 05:03:27 [__init__.py:369] --linear-backend=marlin has no kernel for this linear layer type; using automatic selection for that layer type.
(Worker_TP0 pid=2338534) INFO 10-09 05:04:17 [gpu_worker.py:726] Available KV cache memory: 66.72 GiB
INFO:     Application startup complete.
```

`Available KV cache memory` is printed after the profiling forward pass, which is where it failed before. The logs have no `Traceback` and no `RuntimeError`. As a check of the O-projection output, two requests were sent with temperature 0. A completion of "The capital of France is" returned " Paris…". A chat request, "What is 17 times 23? Answer with the number only.", returned `391`.

| Tree | Attention backend | Runs | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `81198e97b` | default and `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` | 4 (1 editable install, 3 in the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image at the same commit) | all 4 failed with the error above | | with this change | default (FlashMLA) | 2 | both reached `Application startup complete.` and answered correctly | | with this change | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` | 1 | reached `Application startup complete.` and answered correctly |

New unit test, on the same machine:

```bash
pytest tests/quantization/test_fp8.py -k test_fp8_block_bmm_projects_under_linear_backend -v
```

- With the fix: `auto`, `marlin` and `triton` pass.
- Old code (old `fp8.py` and `kernels/linear/__init__.py`, new test): `auto` passes. `marlin` fails with `RuntimeError: Expected size for first two dimensions of batch2 tensor to be: [2, 512] but got: [2, 128].` `triton` fails with `RuntimeError: Assertion error (csrc/apis/../jit_kernels/impls/../heuristics/../../utils/layout.hpp:46): t.dim() == N`.

Nearby tests with the fix: 65 passed, 1 skipped. This includes the existing MXFP8 bmm test, `test_mxfp8_bmm_loads_and_projects_grouped_weights`. The 4 deselected tests download full models.

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_scaled_mm_kernel_selection.py tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py tests/quantization/test_fp8.py \
  -k "not test_model_load_and_run and not test_kv_cache_model_load_and_run and not test_load_fp16_model"
```

`pre-commit` passes on the three changed files. The test is in `tests/quantization/test_fp8.py`, which is already in Buildkite (`check-test-tethering` passed). It skips without CUDA or DeepGEMM. No accuracy eval was run.

## Details

**Root cause.** DeepSeek-V4 builds `wo_a` as a plain `ColumnParallelLinear` and sets `is_bmm = True` after construction. So `Fp8LinearMethod.create_weights` picks `wo_a`'s kernel as for any other linear layer. The model never calls that kernel. `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` reads `wo_a.weight` and its scales directly and runs DeepGEMM's grouped `fp8_einsum`. That needs an FP8 weight in DeepGEMM's `(groups, rank, K)` layout. On CUDA, only `DeepGemmFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` reads `is_bmm` and builds that layout. With the default backend, DeepGEMM comes first, so it works. With `--linear-backend marlin`, Marlin repacks the FP8 `(4096, 4096)` weight into int32 tiles `(256, 16384)`. The O-projection then sees a non-FP8 dtype and takes its bf16 `torch.bmm` branch. There, `view(4, 1024, -1)` gives `[4, 1024, 1024]`, which is 4x too small. Triton and Cutlass leave the weight 2-D, so DeepGEMM asserts `t.dim() == N`.

A debug print at the entry of `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` confirmed this. Before the fix, `wo_a.weight` was `torch.int32 (256, 16384)` with `MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel`. With the fix, it is `torch.float8_e4m3fn (4, 1024, 4096)` with `DeepGemmFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`. The input shape was right (32 local heads = 4 groups x 8 heads).

**Fix.** This follows the ModelOpt MXFP8 path, which already picks the kernel again for `is_bmm` layers in `process_weights_after_loading`.

- `init_fp8_linear_kernel` takes a new `is_bmm` argument. For block FP8 it then uses `_POSSIBLE_FP8_BLOCK_BMM_KERNELS`. On CUDA that list holds only `DeepGemmFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`. Other platforms keep their usual lists, so ROCm, XPU and CPU do not change.
- `Fp8LinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading` picks the kernel again for a block-FP8 `is_bmm` layer, because `is_bmm` is set by then.
- If `--linear-backend` has no kernel in that list, the existing `_resolve_backend_kernels` logs the warning shown above and uses automatic selection for that layer.

**Limitations.**

- With `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` and `--linear-backend marlin`, startup now fails at load with `ValueError: Failed to find a kernel`. Before, it failed at the first forward pass. The message says only Hopper and Blackwell are supported, which is misleading on a B200.
- XPU may have a similar gap. `xpu_sparse.py` reads `wo_a.bmm_weight`, and only `XPUFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` sets it, so `--linear-backend triton` on XPU could fail. This is not changed, because XPU could not be tested here.
- Other quant methods that call `init_fp8_linear_kernel`, for example compressed-tensors FP8 block, do not pick the kernel again for `is_bmm`. No DSV4 checkpoint used here goes through them.
- Not run on GB10 (SM 12.1). `support_deep_gemm` includes the SM 12.x family, so `wo_a` should get DeepGEMM there too.
- `cutlass` and `humming` also failed before and pass now, but they are not in the test. Humming needs an optional package, and Cutlass block support depends on the GPU.

---

nodes.body: [#60891](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60891) fixes the same issue by dequantizing `wo_a` to BF16 in the DSv4 code. Could the description compare against it too, as it does for [#56119](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56119)? That would make clear which fix to land.

> [#60891](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60891) fixes the same issue by dequantizing `wo_a` to BF16 in the DSv4 code. Could the description compare against it too, as it does for [#56119](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56119)? That would make clear which fix to land.

@stecasta Thanks, here's how the two fixes differ.

Both PRs fix the same root cause. `wo_a` is a `ColumnParallelLinear` that is never called. `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` reads `wo_a.weight` directly and expects one of two layouts: a 3D FP8 `(groups, rank, K)` tensor, which only `DeepGemmFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` prepares for `is_bmm` layers, or plain BF16. Any other `--linear-backend` leaves the weight in its own layout: packed int32 for Marlin, 2D FP8 for Triton and Cutlass.

- **This PR ([60920](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60920))** fixes it on the kernel side. For a block-FP8 `is_bmm` layer, it picks the kernel again after loading, and on CUDA only DeepGEMM is allowed. `wo_a` stays FP8 in the same layout and kernel as the default backend, so numerics match `auto`. All other linears still use the requested backend.
- **[60891](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60891)** fixes it on the model side. After loading, it dequantizes `wo_a` to BF16 when the weight is not 3D FP8, and the O-projection then takes the `torch.bmm` branch.

Trade-offs:

- **Memory and speed:** [60891](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60891) holds `wo_a` in BF16, about 0.7 GiB more per GPU at TP=2 in both PRs' measurements, and runs that projection as a BF16 bmm. This PR keeps FP8.
- **RopeQuant:** [60891](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60891) has to recheck `_fuse_rope_quant` on SM100 after the dtype changes. Each attention layer also needs its own hook. This PR leaves the dtype unchanged, so neither is needed.
- **DeepGEMM dependency:** this is where [60891](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60891) is more robust. It works without DeepGEMM. This PR needs DeepGEMM for `wo_a`, so with `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`, or on a build without DeepGEMM, startup fails at load. I'll replace the misleading "only Hopper and Blackwell" error with an explicit one, as you suggested.
- **Scope:** [60891](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60891) touches only DSv4 code and works with any quant method. This PR changes shared FP8 kernel selection and covers `Fp8LinearMethod` only.
To be honest both approached looks good. I am ok to go forward with #60891

Thanks @vadiklyutiy, clear comparison. Agreed on #60891: the issue came from GB10 on the stock aarch64 image, so not depending on DeepGEMM is the safer fix there. I'll review #60891. If it doesn't get engagement, we can go with this one instead.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Hi @vadiklyutiy, IIUC `wo_a` now always needs `DeepGemmFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`, so on Spark it depends on DeepGEMM being present in the aarch64 build. Since the fix wasnt tested on gb10, @ChristosKitsos, could you check that the issue's command starts with this branch? If it still reproduces, we can help collect evidence on Spark.

Minor: with `--linear-backend marlin` this logs "--linear-backend=marlin was requested, but no marlin kernel exists for scaled-mm layers", even though Marlin serves every other FP8 block layer. Since `wo_a` is the only layer that ignores the flag, could this branch log its own message saying that `is_bmm` layers need the DeepGEMM layout?

files.patch:
@@ -600,6 +600,81 @@ def test_mxfp8_bmm_loads_and_projects_grouped_weights(
         torch.testing.assert_close(compiled(inputs), output, rtol=0, atol=0)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="DeepGEMM requires CUDA")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("linear_backend", ["auto", "marlin", "triton"])
+def test_fp8_block_bmm_projects_under_linear_backend(
+    dist_init, default_vllm_config, linear_backend
+):
+    """A block FP8 is_bmm layer (DeepSeek-V4 wo_a) keeps the layout the
+    grouped O-projection reads, whatever --linear-backend picks for linears."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import ColumnParallelLinear
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v4.nvidia.ops.o_proj import (
+        compute_fp8_einsum_recipe,
+        deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj,
+    )
+    from vllm.utils.deep_gemm import is_deep_gemm_supported
+    from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_default_torch_dtype
+
+    if not is_deep_gemm_supported():
+        pytest.skip("DeepSeek-V4 FP8 O-projection requires DeepGEMM")
+
+    default_vllm_config.model_config = SimpleNamespace(
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16, hf_text_config=SimpleNamespace()
+    )
+    default_vllm_config.kernel_config.linear_backend = linear_backend
+    n_groups, rank, k, num_tokens = 2, 128, 512, 7
+    with set_default_torch_dtype(torch.bfloat16), torch.device("cuda"):
+        linear = ColumnParallelLinear(
+            k,
+            n_groups * rank,
+            bias=False,
+            quant_config=Fp8Config(weight_block_size=[128, 128]),
+            return_bias=False,
+        )
+    linear.is_bmm = True
+    linear.bmm_batch_size = n_groups
+    weight = torch.randn(n_groups * rank, k, device="cuda").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    # Powers of two, so DeepGEMM's UE8M0 requantization leaves them unchanged.
+    scales = torch.exp2(
+        torch.randint(-3, 4, (n_groups * rank // 128, k // 128), device="cuda").float()
+    )
+    linear.weight.data.copy_(weight)
+    linear.weight_scale_inv.data.copy_(scales)
+    linear.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(linear)
+
+    x = torch.randn(num_tokens, n_groups, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    # cos = 1 and sin = 0, so the inverse RoPE is the identity.
+    cache = torch.cat(
+        (
+            torch.ones(num_tokens, 32, device="cuda"),
+            torch.zeros(num_tokens, 32, device="cuda"),
+        ),
+        dim=1,
+    )
+    recipe, tma_aligned_scales = compute_fp8_einsum_recipe()
+    projected = deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj(
+        x,
+        torch.arange(num_tokens, device="cuda"),
+        cache,
+        linear,
+        torch.nn.Identity(),
+        n_groups=n_groups,
+        heads_per_group=1,
+        nope_dim=448,
+        rope_dim=64,
+        o_lora_rank=rank,
+        einsum_recipe=recipe,
+        tma_aligned_scales=tma_aligned_scales,
+    )
+    dequant = weight.float() * scales.repeat_interleave(128, 0).repeat_interleave(
+        128, 1
+    )
+    reference = torch.einsum(
+        "tgk,grk->tgr", x.float(), dequant.view(n_groups, rank, k)
+    ).flatten(1)
+    assert (projected.float() - reference).norm() / reference.norm() < 0.06
+

issue_comments.body: [#60891](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60891) fixes the same issue by dequantizing `wo_a` to BF16 in the DSv4 code. Could the description compare against it too, as it does for [#56119](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56119)? That would make clear which fix to land.

> [#60891](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60891) fixes the same issue by dequantizing `wo_a` to BF16 in the DSv4 code. Could the description compare against it too, as it does for [#56119](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56119)? That would make clear which fix to land.

@stecasta Thanks, here's how the two fixes differ.

Both PRs fix the same root cause. `wo_a` is a `ColumnParallelLinear` that is never called. `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` reads `wo_a.weight` directly and expects one of two layouts: a 3D FP8 `(groups, rank, K)` tensor, which only `DeepGemmFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` prepares for `is_bmm` layers, or plain BF16. Any other `--linear-backend` leaves the weight in its own layout: packed int32 for Marlin, 2D FP8 for Triton and Cutlass.

- **This PR ([60920](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60920))** fixes it on the kernel side. For a block-FP8 `is_bmm` layer, it picks the kernel again after loading, and on CUDA only DeepGEMM is allowed. `wo_a` stays FP8 in the same layout and kernel as the default backend, so numerics match `auto`. All other linears still use the requested backend.
- **[60891](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60891)** fixes it on the model side. After loading, it dequantizes `wo_a` to BF16 when the weight is not 3D FP8, and the O-projection then takes the `torch.bmm` branch.

Trade-offs:

- **Memory and speed:** [60891](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60891) holds `wo_a` in BF16, about 0.7 GiB more per GPU at TP=2 in both PRs' measurements, and runs that projection as a BF16 bmm. This PR keeps FP8.
- **RopeQuant:** [60891](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60891) has to recheck `_fuse_rope_quant` on SM100 after the dtype changes. Each attention layer also needs its own hook. This PR leaves the dtype unchanged, so neither is needed.
- **DeepGEMM dependency:** this is where [60891](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60891) is more robust. It works without DeepGEMM. This PR needs DeepGEMM for `wo_a`, so with `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`, or on a build without DeepGEMM, startup fails at load. I'll replace the misleading "only Hopper and Blackwell" error with an explicit one, as you suggested.
- **Scope:** [60891](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60891) touches only DSv4 code and works with any quant method. This PR changes shared FP8 kernel selection and covers `Fp8LinearMethod` only.
To be honest both approached looks good. I am ok to go forward with #60891

Thanks @vadiklyutiy, clear comparison. Agreed on #60891: the issue came from GB10 on the stock aarch64 image, so not depending on DeepGEMM is the safer fix there. I'll review #60891. If it doesn't get engagement, we can go with this one instead.
